title: AAA and distributions — Crane Inc.
instructions: Crane Inc. converted from a C corporation to an S corporation in 2021 and has accumulated E&P of $30,000 from its C years. Its sole shareholder, Mo Crane, has stock basis of $70,000 at January 1, 2025. Crane's AAA at January 1, 2025 is $25,000. Compute the 2025 amounts. No elections are made.

exhibits.title: Crane Inc. — 2025
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Ordinary business income | 80,000 |
| Tax-exempt interest | 5,000 |
| Long-term capital gain | 10,000 |
| Nondeductible fines | 2,000 |
| Cash distributions to Mo | 120,000 |

rows.label: Dividend portion of the distribution
rows.explanation: The next 7,000 comes from accumulated E&P: **7,000** dividend.

rows.label: Mo's stock basis at December 31
rows.explanation: 70,000 + 80,000 + 5,000 + 10,000 = 165,000; − 113,000 AAA distribution = 52,000; − 2,000 nondeductible fines = **50,000**. The dividend portion doesn't reduce basis.

rows.label: Which account tracks Crane's tax-exempt interest?
rows.explanation: Tax-exempt income increases stock basis and OAA, not AAA.

rows.label: Why might Crane elect to distribute E&P before AAA?
options: To eliminate E&P and the passive investment income tax and termination risk
To increase the shareholder's stock basis
rows.answer: To eliminate E&P and the passive investment income tax and termination risk
rows.explanation: A §1368(e)(3) election purges accumulated E&P, removing exposure to the §1375 tax and to termination for excess passive income.
